rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a flat lookup reference page with no guess-before-reveal demo beats anywhere in the body.

Closest call: chunk 19 "19. Long-running shapes: Routines (/schedule)", lines 322-324, is the shortest section (one paragraph) but carries a full self-contained claim (what Routines are, how to invoke, the GitHub-repo requirement) — not a wait-state or context-dependent fragment.

Spot-checked headers against body content across the file, e.g. chunk 38 "38. Monorepo hygiene: `claudeMdExcludes`" (lines 572-591) delivers exactly claudeMdExcludes config + scope; chunk 33 "33. `--append-system-prompt`: system-prompt-level instructions" (450-474) delivers the flag and its family table. No header found that the chunk's own content contradicts.

Mechanical scan of body (grep, maintainer block excluded): zero "Not X. Not Y. Z." constructions, zero self-grading superlatives (`grep -niE "one of the most|the best|extremely|incredibly|the most (useful|important|powerful)"` -> 0 matches), zero "about N%...could be more/less" number-retraction pairs, zero anaphora/epistrophe triples or empty-leg verb triplets found on manual read of all 43 chunks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest call: chunk 19, line 324, "GitHub-event triggers can be attached from either surface" — "surface" as noun. Judged as ordinary engineering usage (interface/channel, akin to "API surface"/"attack surface"), not the repo-internal taxonomy noun ("writing surface") §8 targets; AE101's engineer-IC register clears this. `grep -n "surface"` on the body found no other noun uses; the two verb uses ("surfaces a context reminder", line 538) are explicitly exempted. `beat`, `firing`, `compendium`, `mood`, `forcing function` grepped: zero body hits (compendium: 1 hit, but it's in the maintainer block, exempt).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a lookup surface ("Flat look-up for the primitives AE101 leans on", line 3), so the per-slide bold-count budget is off per §9's explicit reference/supplementary-page waiver. The recurring pattern (bold lead sentence + plain continuation, e.g. line 32 "**`CLAUDE.local.md` is the intended gitignored pattern.**") is consistently applied across all ~40 entries as the file's finding-aid convention, matching the waiver's stated purpose ("a reader arrives with a question and needs to find the row that answers it"). Rule question for the maintainer, not filed as REVISE per dispatch-preamble harm test: a strictly literal reading of the handle-cap sub-clause ("bold the label, not the sentence after it") would flag nearly every entry in this file and its sibling reference pages, degrading an established, deliberate house pattern rather than fixing a comprehension harm — the bolded claim-sentences are exactly what lets a scanning reader find the answer.
